historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run mid-cycle volume + price growth; every trailing CAGR is an artefact of the endpoint's place in the nitrogen cycle
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All CAGRs are cycle-endpoint artefacts: 3-year windows start at the FY2022 super-peak (revenue -14%, EPS -18%), 5-year windows start at the FY2020 trough (revenue +11%, EPS +43%). Equity CAGR (-0.3% / +6.8%) diverges >30% from revenue and EPS on both windows and is further depressed by $5B+ of buybacks since FY2021. None is used as a growth rate; the forward path is a mid-cycle normalisation instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs (after SBC + equity-award taxes) track reported FCF within 0.4pp: SBC is <1% of revenue and not growing faster than cash flow. Equity is total equity incl. NCI as held in Metrics.csv.

scenario_narratives.base: The 2026-27 tightness (constrained global capacity additions, Russian and European supply disruption) fades into a mid-cycle by FY2028 that is structurally better than 2017-20 because European marginal-producer gas stays well above Henry Hub. CF earns ~45% EBITDA margins on ~$7B of revenue (~$3.1B consolidated EBITDA, a notch under management's $2.9B attributable mid-cycle), Blue Point One starts in 2029 roughly on budget, CF's 40% share adds ~$250M revenue at premium low-carbon pricing, and the Yazoo City restart lands in H1-2027. Capex peaks at ~$1B CF-share in 2027-28 and settles near 9% of revenue; buybacks keep the diluted count flat against modest SBC.
scenario_narratives.bull: Nitrogen stays tight longer than 2027: Chinese export restrictions persist, European ammonia capacity keeps closing, and AD/CVD orders keep Russian and Trinidadian UAN out of the US. Low-carbon ammonia premiums (> $20/t today, ~10% of H1-2026 volume) widen as Japanese power and marine-fuel offtake (JERA) materialises, and Blue Point runs full from 2029. Revenue holds ~$7.5-8B through the cycle and margins stay ~48.5%, putting consolidated EBITDA near $3.9-4.3B by 2030 - management's $3.3B attributable 2030 target met and beaten.
scenario_narratives.bear: The two supports that are geopolitical, not structural, unwind together: Russian nitrogen flows normalise (sanctions relief or AD/CVD reviews) and European gas falls back, compressing the global cost curve CF sells into, while US LNG export growth lifts Henry Hub and squeezes CF's own spread from below. Revenue falls to ~$6.2B by FY2028 and margins revert toward the 2017-20 experience at ~37-38%. Blue Point overruns (the Yazoo City slippage is the warning) and its low-carbon premium proves thin, so peak capex runs ~18% of revenue. New CEO and a CFO from outside the industry are learning on the job through the most capital-intensive stretch in a decade.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CF is valued as a mid-cycle nitrogen producer, not on its current-year earnings. The year-1 flow is allowed to run hot on actual H1-2026 results, then everything reverts to a mid-cycle margin and revenue base set a notch below management's raised targets. Risk is carried in the scenario flows and a bear-heavy weighting, not in the discount rate. The CHS minority interest is charged once through a combined tax+NCI leakage rate, and Blue Point is modelled on CF's 40% share only.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is set by the 12x cyclical cap in every scenario; a 10x or 14x exit moves the answer more than any growth or WACC assumption
Mid-cycle margin: each 1pp of mature EBITDA margin is roughly $2-3/share
Henry Hub vs TTF gas spread - the core source of CF's advantage - is exposed to US LNG export growth
Blue Point One cost overrun, delay or thin low-carbon premium; CF-share capex of ~$1B/yr in 2027-28 depends on partner funding continuing
45Q credit and bonus-depreciation policy: the near-term leakage rate assumes both persist
CHS NCI leakage is calibrated on FY2025 (14.9% of EBIT); a different profit mix between CFN and the UK/Blue Point entities shifts it

data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1324404) for FY2007-FY2025 10-Ks and 10-Qs through Q2-2026 (period ended 2026-06-30); Metrics.csv and kpis table in CF.duckdb. Cash (incl. restricted), NCI balance and flows, partner contributions, diluted-share adjustment and cover-page share count pulled from the Q2-2026 10-Q facts.
data_sources.qualitative: research/CF/Reports/CF_Analysis.json (2026-09-26): Q2-2026 results and guidance of 2026-08-06 - ~9.5Mt gross ammonia, ~$1.3B capex incl. ~$600M Blue Point, mid-cycle EBITDA ~$2.9B, 2030 target ~$3.3B, $0.60 quarterly dividend.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 151.338M basic shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (2026-08-03) plus the 0.3M dilutive-securities adjustment from the Q2-2026 diluted EPS reconciliation. Held FLAT because SBC (plus equity-award withholding tax) is expensed in the flows; the $2B buyback programme is the cash mechanism that keeps it flat, so buybacks are value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement: ShareBasedCompensation $45M; plus $14M cash taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing activities). CF publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not deducted: CF is net DEBT ($736M at 2026-06-30), so no cash pile is being counted twice. CF's EBITDA already excludes interest income (it adds back 'interest expense - net').
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock $1,365M (FY2024 $1,509M; H1-2026 $253M). CF is a genuine repurchaser: diluted count fell from ~216M (FY2020) to ~152M, so the flat-count convention is funded, not notional.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity ~9.0% (10y UST ~4.2%, beta ~0.95, ERP 5.0%); pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% on $3.2B senior notes (~4.1% after tax) at ~16% of capital on market values (market cap ~$17.4B). WACC ~8.5%, the SAME in every scenario: nitrogen-price cyclicality, gas-spread risk and Blue Point execution are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked as a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), as filed: US GAAP operating-lease cost (railcars, storage, barges; $421M liability at FY2025) is already expensed inside EBITDA, so lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. No IFRS-16 flattering of FCF.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows. (1) CHS Inc.'s ~11% membership interest in CF Industries Nitrogen LLC: its profit share (FY2025 $343M = 14.9% of consolidated EBIT of $2,300M) is folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax+NCI leakage rate (~32-36%). Calibration: FY2025 EBIT 2,300 x (1 - 0.34) = 1,518 vs attributable net earnings 1,455 + after-tax net interest ~58 = 1,513. (2) Blue Point One JV (CF 40% / JERA 35% / Mitsui 25%, consolidated by CF): modelled PROPORTIONATELY - revenue, EBITDA and capex paths carry only CF's 40% share, since the partners fund their 60% via NCI contributions ($291M FY2025, $233M H1-2026). Consequently the NCI balance ($3,172M at 2026-06-30) is NOT deducted in the bridge; doing so would charge it twice. Small over-charge accepted: the 14% CHS leakage is applied to CF's Blue Point share too (~7% of mature EBITDA).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with cyclical mid-cycle normalisation (routing row 'operating company, cyclical'; owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md read in full). First valuation of CF - no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF. CF is a commodity nitrogen producer: FY2022 revenue was $11.2B and FY2017 $4.1B on essentially the same asset base, so neither the latest year nor any CAGR is a usable base. Driver paths start from FY2026 (year 1, running above mid-cycle on H1-2026 revenue +18% y/y and 57% H1 EBITDA margin) and revert by FY2028 to a mid-cycle ~45% EBITDA margin on ~$6.9B revenue (~$3.1B consolidated EBITDA) - slightly BELOW management's raised $2.9B attributable (~$3.25B consolidated) mid-cycle figure, deliberately. EBITDA margin paths are CF's reported EBITDA (which is after SBC) grossed up for SBC, since the engine deducts SBC separately. FY0 = FY2025 so FY2026 is year 1; because the 30-Jun-2026 cash balance already contains H1-2026 cash generation, the equity bridge deducts ~$880M of realised H1-2026 attributable owner FCF to avoid counting it twice (it is also inside the modelled FY2026 flow). Terminal: the 12x cyclical cap binds in every scenario (Gordon at 8.5%/2% is ~15.7x), so terminal growth barely moves value - the cap is the operative assumption (~6x terminal EBITDA). Cash is cash + restricted cash ($2,480M, 2026-06-30 10-Q); total debt is senior notes $3,216M.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 ~$8.1B: H1 $4,208M actual plus H2 ~10% above H2-2025's $3,531M. Reverts to ~$6.9B by FY2028 as the tight 2026-27 market (management: tight through 2027) normalises. FY2029-30 add CF's 40% share of Blue Point One (1.4Mt low-carbon ammonia, ~$250M proportional revenue at full rate) and the Yazoo City restart (H1-2027). Then ~2.5%: ~1% volume, ~1.5% price.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 ~50% (H1 57.7%, H2 assumed ~46% like H2-2025). Mid-cycle 45% from FY2028: FY2023-25 averaged 46%, FY2017-20 averaged ~35% in a pre-2022 world of cheap European gas. The 45% gives ~$3.1B consolidated EBITDA vs management's $2.9B attributable (~$3.25B consolidated) mid-cycle and $3.3B 2030 target; the house base sits a notch below management.
base.capex_rationale: CF-share capex. FY2026 ~$940M: guided $1.3B total of which ~$600M Blue Point (gross; CF funds 40%, partners 60% via NCI contributions). FY2027-28 peak Blue Point spend (~$1.1B/yr gross, $450M CF share) on top of ~$575-600M sustaining. From FY2030 ~9% of revenue (~$650-750M): sustaining capex ran $400-550M through FY2017-24 on an asset base now ageing plus DEF/CCS projects.
base.da_rationale: D&A ~$900M flat in dollars (FY2025 $898M) plus CF's share of Blue Point from 2029, trending to 10.5% of revenue by year 10 so the perpetuity does not capitalise a D&A tax shield ~$250M above capex forever.
base.tax_rationale: Combined cash tax + CHS NCI leakage on EBIT. Cash taxes ~18% of EBIT near term (FY2025 cash taxes $321M vs $441M provision: 100% bonus depreciation on Blue Point and 45Q credits on Donaldsonville CCS) plus ~14% CHS share. Rises to 36% by FY2035 as bonus depreciation fades and 45Q (12-year credit from 2025) approaches expiry, so the terminal year is post-credit.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer/distributor: receivables + inventory exceed payables and customer prepayments, so growth consumes cash (negative capture) and the FY2027-28 revenue normalisation releases some.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the valuation is struck near the top of the cycle (H1-2026 EBITDA margin 57.7%) and the bear case only needs mean reversion plus normalisation of geopolitical supply disruption - no single failure. Base 50% as the central mid-cycle path anchored a notch below management's own mid-cycle figure. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things at once: prolonged global tightness, durable low-carbon premiums, and on-time Blue Point delivery under new leadership.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
